evals.prompt: Run mutation testing on my changes.
evals.expected_output: Preflights (config present, tool available, tree clean in targets, baseline suite green with wall-clock recorded, the `git status --porcelain` Phase 0 snapshot captured, and the tool's write regime resolved from the project's config), scopes to changed lines vs the configured diff-target, applies the arid suppression record, selects covering tests ONCE and caches the selection, reports the planned scope and estimated cost before running, generates at most one mutant per changed line, executes with guaranteed revert and verifies restoration against the Phase 0 snapshot at the earliest point the resolved regime permits, delegates survivor triage to a fresh-context subagent, and reports per file ranked by oracle gap. Writes no tests, and either leaves tracked source byte-identical or ends in failure naming what it could not restore.

evals.prompt: There are uncommitted edits in the file I want to mutate. Go ahead and run it.
evals.expected_output: Hard-stops at preflight rather than proceeding. Explains that the harness reverts by restoring a known state, so uncommitted edits in the target make revert ambiguous and risk discarding the user's work. Asks them to commit or stash. Does not proceed with a warning, and does not stash on the user's behalf.

evals.prompt: Seven mutants survived. Which ones matter?
evals.expected_output: Delegates the productive / arid / equivalent classification to a fresh-context (non-fork) subagent rather than judging in the authoring context, naming this as the self-grade bias class. Hands over the artifact (mutated line, surrounding code, covering tests), not the reasoning that produced the mutants. Prefers a cross-vendor advisor for the equivalence call when one is installed, with the same-vendor fresh-context subagent as the stated fallback. Reports any WITHHOLDING claim that cannot cite its evidence as unclassified rather than as the class claimed — equivalence without a differential demonstration, and aridity without a complete proposed suppression entry whose `claim` binds a node kind from the closed enumerated vocabulary AND whose `reason` names the behavior the suite deliberately does not assert on. Free prose in `claim` fails the test even when the entry is otherwise complete and the reason is good: a survivor fitting no node kind is not arid.

evals.prompt: Just fix the surviving mutants for me.
evals.expected_output: Reports the survivors and delegates test authoring to /testing:write when the testing plugin is installed, or hands the survivor list back for the user's own conventions when it is not. Does not author tests inside this skill. Explains that verification is re-running the audit scoped to that file, because the harness re-running the mutant is what stops the test author from grading its own work.

evals.prompt: Run it across the whole repo.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes --full as expensive, computes and states the estimated wall-clock from baseline-suite-ms times the mutant count, and confirms before running rather than starting silently. If a cap truncates the mutant set, reports what was dropped so a truncated run does not read as a clean one.

evals.prompt: The mutation run crashed halfway through.
evals.expected_output: Compares the after-state against the Phase 0 `git status --porcelain` snapshot rather than asserting a clean tree, so unrelated work in progress does not produce a false restore failure, and treats any difference in a TRACKED path as a failed restore -- tracked rather than merely mutated, since an adjacent modified tracked file breaks the same invariant, while untracked scratch output does not. Scopes WHEN the comparison runs to the resolved write regime rather than promising a per-revert check everywhere: after every revert only where mutants are applied to tracked source one at a time (`tool: manual`, with the trap's exit paths carrying it too, since a trap fires outside the loop); once at the end where the tool writes out of tree or rewrites the working file whole. Explains that under mutant schemata there is no per-mutant revert to observe -- the tool writes every mutant once and selects one at run time -- so an end-of-run comparison loses nothing there, and never substitutes the tool's own exit status for the comparison. A failed restore is TERMINAL in every regime: no further mutants, no triage, no ranked report, and no findings file even under --persist-findings. Returns a failure verdict naming every unrestored path and the recovery command instead of a normal-looking outcome, citing the liveness-assertion contract's fail-loud rule -- persisting there would hand an apply relay findings whose `Location`s assert a restored tree while tracked source sits mutated. Distinguishes this from a partial run: mutants that never ran are named as not-run, but a run cut short by a failed restore reports failure, not a partial result.

evals.prompt: Which files should I fix first?
evals.expected_output: Ranks by oracle gap as defined once in principles/reference/metrics.md -- `mutation score - code coverage` -- ascending, most negative first, because a large negative gap is the exercised-but-not-checked direction. Does not restate or invert the formula. Explains that the top row is where the reader's belief about the suite is most wrong, and that a file at 30% coverage and 30% score has an honest problem already visible in a coverage report while a file at 95% coverage and 45% score is the one lying to them.

evals.prompt: Show me what got suppressed this run.
evals.expected_output: Emits both suppression sections: every applied entry with its reason, date, and contributing layer, AND every entry that did not apply -- personal-only-not-applied with promotion named as the remedy, malformed with the missing key or constituent/key hash mismatch named, and stale entries whose finding is gone or whose operator was retired. Treats these as contract obligations rather than optional report detail, since a suppression the contract declined to enact matters as much as one that applied.

evals.prompt: Run mutation testing on my changes and leave the findings somewhere the fix pass can pick them up.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as the --persist-findings path and runs Phase 6 after reporting. Reads the detector-findings producer contract at its raw-URL citation before the first write rather than inventing the destination. Resolves the findings location by running the whole rung order, not only the documented default, and runs the self-ignore guard on the RESOLVED memory root -- where a checkout governs that root -- without ever editing the consumer's root .gitignore, and does not run it at all where no checkout governs the destination. Writes exactly one file named `<UTC-basic-timestamp>-mutation-survivors.md`, and when that path already exists writes `-2`, then `-3`, taking the smallest free integer >= 2 rather than overwriting. Sets frontmatter `branch:` to `git branch --show-current` verbatim rather than the directory slug. Emits `Location` as a repo-relative `file:line` for the mutated line, `Surface(s)` as `mutation-testing:audit`, and escapes literal pipes in the `Finding` and `Action` cells because mutation fragments carry them. Names the covering test file inside `Action` and states that the remediation site is NOT the row's `Location` -- a mutation finding's fix lands in the test, not at the mutated node, and a consumer that fences each fix to `Location` would otherwise have to guess the target or breach its own fence. Does not restate the findings-file table anywhere.

evals.prompt: Run the mutation audit on this diff.
evals.expected_output: Runs Phases 0-5 and stops. Persists no findings file: the flag is opt-in and bare invocation is report-and-stop. Leaves `git status --porcelain` matching the Phase 0 snapshot with no memory-tier write at all.

evals.prompt: Three mutants survived with --persist-findings on: one productive, one arid with a complete proposed suppression entry whose claim names a node kind from the vocabulary and whose reason names the specific behavior the suite leaves unasserted, one you called equivalent but could not demonstrate. What lands in the file?
evals.expected_output: Emits exactly two rows -- the productive survivor and the undemonstrated-equivalence survivor, both IMPORTANT, both `Confidence: high`. Names the class-keyed map as the source of the tier and does not re-derive severity from the finding's wording. Explains that productive is IMPORTANT rather than CRITICAL because a survivor proves the suite is blind, not that the source produces a wrong result, and that the unclassified survivor ranks WITH productive rather than below it so an undemonstrated equivalence claim cannot bury a real gap. Emits NO row for the DEMONSTRATED arid survivor, because its only remediation is a suppression entry the user must accept and handing that to an apply relay would launder the consent gate -- while still showing it to the human in the Phase 5 report; an aridity claim with no complete proposed suppression entry binding a node kind is unclassified instead and emits. Never emits `Confidence: low`, which ranks below omitting the field.

evals.prompt: I ran it with --persist-findings and nothing survived. Did it write a file? And does this still count as a read-only audit?
evals.expected_output: Answers both. (1) Yes, if at least one mutant was examined: the file is written with the `## Findings` header row and no data rows, because the payload is the `## Surfaces` line and the consumer unions `## Surfaces` across producers -- a surface that ran and returned nothing is coverage information a silent run destroys. If NO mutant was examined (empty scope, everything dropped by coverage/suppression/cap, or a Phase 0 refusal) it writes nothing, because claiming the surface ran would fabricate coverage never attempted. (2) Yes: the invariant is read-only with respect to TRACKED SOURCE, which stays byte-identical; the opt-in writes land in a memory tier proven to sit outside tracked space and are the explicit user override the naming doctrine's verb table already sanctions. If the destination cannot be PROVEN outside tracked space -- the probe reports it tracked, the probe could not evaluate the path, the self-ignore guard could not be established, or the resolved root is invalid -- it does not write, and reports which of those it was rather than collapsing them.

evals.prompt: Our memory_dir points at a shared directory outside this worktree. Will --persist-findings write there?
evals.expected_output: Yes, once EACH write the phase makes -- the findings file, and the self-ignore guard's `.gitignore` where a governing checkout was found -- is proven outside tracked space before THAT write is made (per-write, not both up front, since on a fresh root the guard's file is what makes the findings file's probe pass). Where NO governing checkout is found, the guard does not run at all and the findings file is the only write: there is no repository to keep it out of, and the guard's create-when-absent rule could otherwise land on a `.gitignore` absent from disk but tracked in an undiscovered checkout, modifying committed content with the tracked-file check never having run. Makes the resolved root physical first via `pwd -P` from its nearest existing ancestor, so a symlinked ancestor cannot hide a checkout. Then resolves the governing checkout from TWO signals that must BOTH come back empty before the permissive branch: a walk of that physical path's ancestors for a `.git` entry using `test -e` (not `-d`, since a worktree's `.git` is a file), AND `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` run under the AMBIENT environment. Neither alone: rev-parse cannot distinguish no-repository from a missing directory, a dangling gitdir, or a discovery limit such as GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES -- all exit 128 -- while the walk cannot see a working tree designated by GIT_WORK_TREE or GIT_DIR. Names `core.worktree` as a topology defeating both signals, and says the permissive branch is SHAPED around it rather than merely disclosing it -- skipping the guard is what makes that topology harmless, since the findings file alone overwrites nothing there. With a governing checkout T: rejects a root-equivalent memory_dir judged against T; proves the guard's write BEFORE the guard makes it via `git -C T ls-files -- <resolved root>`, requiring exit 0 AND empty output -- a fatal ls-files prints nothing to stdout and exits 128, so reading output alone lets a failure pass for a clean root; only then runs the guard and `git -C T check-ignore -q -- <intended file path>`, writing only on exit 0. Reports exit 1 ('the destination is tracked space') distinctly from any other exit ('the probe did not evaluate this path'), refusing on both. Anchors the probes to a governing checkout, never the invoking worktree, because check-ignore against an outside path is fatal with exit 128 -- a worktree-anchored probe would refuse every write in a layout the fanout fix action supports explicitly -- and notes that `git -C` alone is not an anchor, since GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE override it. Not a path-prefix comparison, which would need BOTH paths canonicalized where realpath and readlink's canonicalizing flag are GNU-only.

evals.prompt: Our tool rewrites the source file in place, one mutant at a time, and has no reporter API. Will this run?
evals.expected_output: No -- Phase 0 REFUSES rather than running with a weaker gate. Identifies the regime as in-tree per mutant, the one regime where pile-on is real: a failed revert leaves the next mutant landing on unrestored source and every later verdict describing a tree nobody wrote. That regime's gate is a comparison after every revert, and with no per-mutant observability and no interrupt safety the gate cannot be run at all -- a check that cannot run is not a check, so the skill stops instead of reporting an outcome it cannot vouch for. Does not silently downgrade to an end-of-run comparison, which would leave the pile-on undetectable while the run reads as normal. Resolves the regime from the project's own config rather than from the tool's reputation, and states the resolved regime in the scope report. Contrast it draws correctly: a tool that writes mutants out of tree, or rewrites the working file whole once, is gated by an end-of-run comparison and runs fine -- the refusal is specific to per-mutant in-tree writing without observability, not to in-tree writing as such.
